explanation: More than a quarter of all the member states of the United Nations are African countries.

claims.text: Africa has more countries than any other continent.
Asia, Europe and South America each have fewer countries than Africa.
More than a quarter of the member states of the United Nations are in Africa.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: content:check reports no errors and one C22 warning: the same answer as p.food.0250, which asks where watermelons were domesticated, a different fact; related, not a duplicate, for the editor to confirm with related_ok. Claims: every checkable statement is listed, distractors included; c1 (superlative) and c3 (number) are high under the C26 floor, and c2 is standard. Datasets: mledoze-countries, independent entries by region: Africa 54, Asia 46, Europe 45, Americas 35 (South America 12 of them), Oceania 14 (c1, c2). unMember entries in Africa: 54. The file counts 194 UN members because it wrongly marks Vatican City as one; against the real total of 193, 54 is 28%, and against 194 it is still over a quarter (c3). Rival test: Asia is the big continent and Europe has many small states, so both tempt. Against the key: totals for Asia and Europe move with how countries that span both are counted, but no convention lifts either near Africa's. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: Nobody's local knowledge; players reason from what they know of each continent's map. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight apostrophes, explanation of 16 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. External evidence: none beyond the dataset. Seed: 3 (medium): many players guess Asia or Europe. Counterintuitive: false. Doubts: c3 avoids the exact count, which would change if a new African state joined the UN.

evidence.excerpt: AF 54, AS 46, EU 45, NA 23, OC 15, SA 12

claimResults.note: Africa leads under this continent column, and also in mledoze-countries' regions (Africa 54, Asia 46, Europe 45). Any continent model puts it ahead.
54 of the 193 UN members is 28%, more than a quarter. The file counts 194 members because it marks Vatican City as one (manifest known issue); that does not change the African count.

evidence.excerpt: UN members by region in the pinned file: Africa 54, Asia 46, Europe 45, Americas 35 (South America 12), Oceania 14.

claimResults.note: High-risk superlative checked against the dataset. Africa leads by 8 even if Russia, Egypt and Turkiye are counted in both of their continents (Asia 46 plus 2 is still below 54), and with the 5-continent model (Americas 35). Counting-convention issue recorded below.

evidence.excerpt: South America 12 UN members, Europe 45, Asia 46, against Africa 54.

claimResults.note: Each option has fewer than Africa under every common convention that keeps Europe and Asia apart.

evidence.excerpt: 54 African UN members of 194 flagged (193 once Vatican City is removed, as its knownIssues say): 27.8% to 28.0%, above a quarter.

claimResults.note: The pinned file counts Vatican City as a UN member; either denominator gives more than 25%.

issues.note: Counting convention (guide 3.2): the key holds with Europe and Asia counted separately, as the options do, and with the five-continent model. It would fail only if Europe and Asia were merged into Eurasia, which no option offers, so one answer holds. No change needed.

editor.reason: Both checks pass with every claim confirmed; high-risk c1 (country-codes and mledoze-countries) and c3 (mledoze-countries) carry dataset evidence in a confirming check (§9.9 rule 3). Lint clean, no myth hits. B's counting-convention note holds the key under every model the options use. Dedupe: p.food.0250 asks where watermelons were domesticated, a different fact, so related_ok.

stem: Which continent is home to more independent countries than any other?
